101.title: The One Person Company Blueprint
101.subtitle: Niche, Offer and Business Foundations
101.tag: Design a one person business the market has already asked for: a validated niche, a tested brand promise, priced services, and the legal foundations to trade.
101.audience: Professionals planning a move into self employment, career transitioners exploring a solo venture, and freelancers who want to move from ad hoc gigs to a structured business.
overview: Most solo businesses fail before they start: built on an untested idea, priced by guesswork, and structured as an afterthought. AOP 101 runs the foundation work properly, in five consecutive days, with a deliverable gate at the end of each one. You do not move on until the asset is built.

The course applies the operator method from Kydon's flagship One Person Company programme: every concept is applied immediately on a real business. Participants with a venture of their own work on it directly; everyone else builds on Brightleaf Bookkeeping, the fully prepared reference business supplied in the starter pack, so no exercise ever runs on a blank page.
los: Select and validate a business niche using the 3S Filter and real market evidence
Build evidence backed customer personas and a competitor gap analysis
Write a brand promise that passes four quality checks and survives customer scrutiny
Construct an indicative pricing model grounded in client return on investment and revenue per hour
Choose a business entity structure and prepare a draft service agreement covering IP and data
outline: The operator mindset, opportunity discovery, and the 3S Filter. Participants leave with a scored niche shortlist.
Synthetic personas, pain point mapping, and competitor intelligence. Evidence replaces assumption.
The brand promise formula, four quality checks, and unit economics. A promise reaches version three or better.
Entity choices, the entity decision memo, and a draft service agreement with personalised IP and data clauses.
Each participant presents the full foundation to a panel and receives written feedback against five criteria.
builds: A validated niche statement with 3S Filter scorecard
Three evidence backed personas and a problem validation report
A brand promise at version three or better with an indicative pricing model
An entity decision memo and draft service agreement
assess: Project
Blueprint portfolio, 3 hours. The complete foundation set assessed against published criteria.
Oral Interview
Panel presentation, 1 hour. The blueprint defended live before a panel, with written feedback.
101.disclaim: Day 4 provides awareness and structured reasoning on legal and entity matters, not legal advice. Participants are directed to qualified professionals for jurisdiction specific decisions.

102.title: AI Agents at Work
102.subtitle: Build Your First AI Workforce with Claude
102.tag: Move from chatting with AI to running it. Build two working AI agents on real business tasks and learn to choose the right model for each job.
102.audience: Business owners, solo operators, and professionals who use AI casually and want repeatable, dependable AI agents doing defined jobs in their work.
overview: Almost everyone can prompt an AI model. Very few can make it do a defined job reliably, again and again, without supervision of every word. AOP 102 closes that gap in two intensive days: you learn how frontier models actually differ, how to match the model to the task, and how to structure an agent as a persistent, tested working asset rather than a disposable chat.

By the final afternoon you sit a live practical exam: building and stress testing an agent under time conditions, against real inputs, marked against published criteria. Participants without their own business work on Brightleaf Bookkeeping, the reference business supplied in the starter pack.
los: Compare frontier AI models against defined business tasks and record a selection rationale
Distinguish a persistent AI agent from a disposable chat and structure agents as saved projects
Build two focused, single purpose AI agents grounded in real business context
Test agent output quality and iterate context until output is dependable
Produce a model comparison card that guides every future build decision
outline: How large language models differ, fit to function selection, and the model comparison card built on live tasks.
Two working agents built as persistent projects, tested against real inputs, with a documented context structure. Closes with the live practical exam.
builds: Two working, tested AI agents built on real business tasks
A documented agent context structure reusable for future agents
assess: Practical Exam
Live agent build and test, 2 hours. An agent built, stress tested and hardened under exam conditions against published marking criteria.
related: Where the agents go to work

103.title: The Knowledge Advantage
103.subtitle: RAG Knowledge Bases and Your AI Team
103.tag: Models are rented and identical. Your captured knowledge is the moat. Build a retrieval ready knowledge base and an eight function AI team that answers from your facts, under your supervision.
103.audience: Operators and small teams already using AI tools who need consistency, accuracy, and control across every AI output the business produces.
overview: Every business using AI hits the same wall: outputs that sound confident but do not know your facts, your voice, or your standards. AOP 103 solves it by building the missing layer: a live, retrieval ready knowledge base and a team of eight agents wired to answer from it, each with human-in-the-loop checkpoints so nothing reaches a customer without your approval.

Over three days you design the full AI team blueprint across eight business functions, build the knowledge base in Notion, connect every agent to a shared voice and standards page, and persona test each one. The course closes with a live team demonstration and a written quality standards document, both formally assessed. Participants without their own business build on the Brightleaf Bookkeeping reference business.
los: Explain retrieval augmented generation and structure a Notion knowledge base for clean retrieval
Design an AI team blueprint across eight business functions with four decisions per function
Wire agents to a shared knowledge base and a shared voice and standards page
Build human-in-the-loop checkpoints so every agent escalates defined decisions to the operator
Test each agent against a customer persona and document a written quality standard
outline: Agent versus prompt, the AI team blueprint, human-in-the-loop supervision, and knowledge as the moat.
Build the live RAG knowledge base in Notion and wire the first three agents with review and approve checkpoints.
Complete all eight agents on a shared voice and standards page, persona test each one, and run the gaps audit. Closes with the assessed team demonstration.
builds: An AI team blueprint covering eight business functions
A live, retrieval ready knowledge base in Notion
Eight knowledge connected agents with human-in-the-loop checkpoints and a shared voice standard
assess: Practical Exam
Agent team demonstration, 2 hours. The wired team shown answering from the knowledge base, live.
Project
Quality standards document, 1 hour. The written standard every agent output is held to.

104.title: Automate the Business
104.subtitle: n8n Workflows, Integration and the Without-You Test
104.tag: Reclaim your hours. Build no code n8n workflows that pull from your knowledge base, route output through your approval, and fail loudly instead of silently. Then prove the whole stack runs without you.
104.audience: Operators and business teams ready to automate repeatable work: marketing content, client onboarding, and publishing, with human approval gates kept in place.
overview: Automation fails in business for two reasons: workflows that were never connected to real knowledge, and workflows that break silently. AOP 104 teaches you to build against both. Across four days you build three live n8n workflows, including the signature Marketing RAG Workflow that connects a form trigger, knowledge retrieval, AI drafting and human approval routing into one system.

The course ends on the Without-You Test: the whole stack, models, agents, knowledge and workflows, demonstrated running as one system with you supervising rather than operating. It is assessed live, followed by an oral walkthrough of the stack. Participants without a knowledge base of their own start from the pre built Brightleaf stack supplied in the starter pack. This course is delivered with a specialist automation trainer.
los: Design workflow architecture with triggers, actions, and human approval gates
Build the signature Marketing RAG Workflow connecting forms, knowledge retrieval, AI drafting, and approval routing
Build a client onboarding workflow and a content publishing workflow in n8n
Stress test workflows for reliability, estimate running costs, and design for loud failure
Integrate models, agents, knowledge, and workflows into one system and apply the Without-You Test
outline: How automation actually works, n8n orientation, building for reliability, and design for loud failure.
The Marketing RAG Workflow built end to end, then a client onboarding workflow, both with live approval gates.
A third workflow, stress testing all three, and a full running cost audit across the stack.
Orchestration across agents and workflows, observability and monitoring, and the Without-You Test applied formally.
builds: Three live, documented n8n workflows including the Marketing RAG Workflow
A stress test log and running cost estimate for the full automation stack
An orchestration map and a completed Without-You Test scorecard
assess: Practical Exam
Live workflow demonstration, 3 hours. The workflows run against real inputs with approval gates and failure handling proven.
Oral Interview
Stack walkthrough, 1 hour. Every design decision in the stack explained and defended.

105.title: Validate, Price and Sell
105.subtitle: From Offer to Pipeline
105.tag: The line between a job and a business is a paying client. Turn capability into a priced, outcome led offer, validate it with real prospects, and launch a repeatable sales pipeline.
105.audience: Founders, freelancers, and operators with a working capability who have not yet converted it into consistent, qualified sales conversations.
overview: Capability does not pay. Clients do. AOP 105 is four days of turning what you can do into what someone will buy: a priced, outcome led one page offer, validated in structured conversations with real prospects, not friends, then pushed into a live pipeline through a personalised four touch outreach sequence.

The labs run on your real offer and real prospects; the outreach is drafted, approved and sent live in class, and the course is assessed on the evidence: your offer and validation log as a project, and your pipeline defended in an oral review. Participants without an offer of their own work the method on the Brightleaf reference business as the worked demonstration.
los: Define a minimum viable offer priced on outcomes rather than hours
Pre validate an offer through structured conversations with real prospects and log the signals
Build a targeted prospect list using ideal customer profile filters in Apollo
Design and launch a personalised four touch outreach sequence
Run a pipeline tracker, qualify replies honestly, and book real sales conversations
outline: Outcome led offers, pricing on value, the one page offer, and the first client shortlist.
Structured validation conversations with real prospects, signal logging, and the go or refine decision.
Go-to-market for a small operation, ideal customer profiles, and a targeted Apollo list of around 25 prospects.
The four touch sequence launched live, objection handling, qualification, and pipeline review.
builds: A validation log of at least five real prospect conversations
A launched four touch sequence with a populated pipeline tracker and at least one booked conversation
assess: Project
Offer and validation log, 2 hours. The priced offer and evidence of real validation conversations, assessed against published criteria.
Oral Interview
Pipeline review, 2 hours. The live pipeline walked through and every qualification decision defended.

106.title: Launch Ready
106.subtitle: Registration, Money and the Readiness Check
106.tag: A business is structure, not just revenue. Register it, get paid properly, build unit economics that survive stress testing, and prove launch readiness in front of a panel.
106.audience: Operators with demand in hand who now need the legal, financial, and operational structure of a real business, built and checked before launch.
overview: Demand without structure is a hobby with invoices. AOP 106 is three days of making the business real: entity options assessed and the registration prepared, a live payment capability with an invoicing cadence, unit economics stress tested against fewer clients and churn, and a money system with separated accounts, tax set aside and a weekly numbers check.

The course closes on the launch readiness check across legal, financial, operational and commercial dimensions, presented to a panel. Participants without their own venture run the full method on the Brightleaf reference business supplied in the starter pack.
los: Assess entity options and prepare a business registration, with awareness of when professional advice is required
Set up a live payment capability and an invoicing cadence
Build a unit economics model and stress test it against fewer clients and churn
Set up a money system: separated accounts, tax set aside, and a weekly numbers check
Complete a launch readiness check across legal, financial, operational, and commercial dimensions and present it to a panel
outline: Entity options assessed, the registration prepared, and a live payment capability with an invoicing cadence.
Unit economics, break even, sensitivity and stress testing, and the one page business plan.
The money system, the launch readiness checklist, and a panel presentation of the launch ready business.
builds: A registered or registration ready entity with live payment capability
A stress tested unit economics model and one page business plan
A completed launch readiness checklist presented to a panel
assess: Project
Unit economics and plan, 2 hours. The stress tested model and one page plan assessed against published criteria.
Oral Interview
Readiness panel, 2 hours. The launch ready business presented and defended before a panel.
106.disclaim: This course provides awareness and structured reasoning, not legal, tax, or accounting advice. Participants with work passes, partners, or foreign income are directed to qualified professionals before registering.

102.title: AI at Work
102.subtitle: From Awareness to Action
102.tag: A two day hands on workshop for every level of the organisation: understand what AI actually is, use it on your real work all day, and leave with a personal 90 day action roadmap and seven working outputs.
102.metaDescription: A two day hands on AI workshop for teams: prompt skills on real work, seven usable outputs per participant, and a personal 90 day AI action roadmap. Delivered in person by Future Edge Institute.

102.audience: Executives, managers and operational staff across every function. Designed for teams adopting AI together, and no technical background is needed.
overview: The principle is simple: people learn by doing, not watching. The facilitator talks for less than a third of the time and participants build for the rest. No activity uses a fictional case study. Every output produced across the two days comes from each participant's actual work, which is why everyone leaves with seven real, usable assets rather than notes.

Across five modules participants learn what AI actually is and where it fits their role, practise structured prompting on their own writing, analysis and communication tasks, produce a complete multimedia communication brief, prototype an improvement to a real workflow, and build a personal 90 day AI Action Roadmap committed to publicly before the room.
